answer:
A windowed row differs from a normal compact row in three ways, all in `emitLineRow` (src/out_json.zig:233-279):

1. **Kind tag suffix:** a `w` is appended to the kind code (after the optional `v` for inverted), e.g. `"mw"` instead of `"m"` (src/out_json.zig:241-244).

2. **Text:** the text element is the window bytes (`w.bytes`) instead of the full line text (src/out_json.zig:256).

3. **Two extra trailing elements:** the window start offset (`w.start`) and the full line length (`ev.text.len`) (src/out_json.zig:268-273). The comment says the `w` row "carries two extra elements after the text" (src/out_json.zig:242-243).

Additionally, the match position inside the text is shifted by the window start (`sp.start - w.start`) when checking whether the match is derivable from the text (src/out_json.zig:261). If it is not derivable, the match string is emitted explicitly (src/out_json.zig:264-267).

The window only applies when `max_columns > 0` and `windowOf` returns a window (src/out_json.zig:154). Otherwise the row is unchanged.

The context shows only the code path. A row with no match span (`ev.span == null`) emits just the full `ev.text`, with no window fields, even though the `w` suffix may still be set (src/out_json.zig:244, 274-277).
